name: Meta-World
summary: Meta-World provides 50 simulated tabletop manipulation tasks sharing a single robot, action space and observation format, grouped into explicit train/test splits designed to measure generalization to unseen tasks rather than mastery of seen ones. It became the standard testbed for multi-task and meta-reinforcement learning, and its ML10 and ML45 splits are still the reference numbers in that literature.
innovation: A shared action and observation space across 50 tasks, so transfer is measurable instead of confounded by differing interfaces.
Explicit held-out task splits, which made 'does multi-task training generalize' a testable question.
matters: Forced multi-task claims to be evaluated on held-out tasks, changing what counted as evidence of generalization.
limits: Simulated, single-arm, with hand-shaped reward functions.
Later shown to be quite sensitive to implementation and reward details, which muddied cross-paper comparison.
lineage: An early standardized MuJoCo suite that defined how multi-task manipulation gets measured.
